name: Super
description: Horizontal dash on the ground, then jump while the dash still touches the ground. The jump is the super (Movement.CheckForSuperJump): the ground jump's 805 up plus 900 sideways momentum (dashJumpMagnitude) the way the stick points.
note: The overlay's SUPER JUMP: a jump in a ground dash (Movement.CheckForSuperJump). The wiki's dash jump.

name: High super
description: Omnidash with one dash (no Vman second dash needed): dash up-diagonal from the ground and jump in the dash, on any of its first 6 dash ticks. The dash lifts off, but onGround lasts through the coyote frames, so the jump is still a super (CheckForSuperJump): 805 up and 900 sideways momentum (dashJumpMagnitude) the stick's way, taken from as high as the dash got (129 u above the floor on dash tick 6), and the jump gives the dash back. The dash stays active under the super, so its end (endDash, dash tick 11) multiplies Velocity by 0.35 as after any up-dash; the later the jump, the less that cut takes. From standing, jump held: dash tick 1 peaks 167 u up, dash tick 6 232 u, a flat super 240 u, all about as far sideways.
note: Omnidash outside Vman: the statue's (it trades a double jump for it); Vman's free box (buyomni) gives it with the one dash too. Demo (Course 1 WJ_DS quick restart, omnidash on): 10 ticks standing, dash up-left with jump on dash tick 6 and the stick up-left through the dash, then hold left with jump held. The overlay's HIGH SUPER: a super whose dash goes up (dashDirection.y > 0). The 1x probe and the offline engine match.

name: Wallbounce
description: Omnidash: an up-diagonal dash into a wall arms wallBouncePossible; a buffered jump there is the wallbounce (FixedUpdate's wall branch): endDash without the vertical cap, SpecialWallJump(1, wallBounceMovementLock 1, up * 220): Velocity (460 away from the wall, 730 up), a 5-tick lock, 220 momentum up, and 120 more momentum away from the wall (wallBounceMagnitude (-120, 220)). A superbounce gives 410 up but only 276 across and a 3-tick lock.
note: The overlay's WALL BOUNCE: the game's wallBouncePossible, an up-diagonal dash into a wall and jump (SpecialWallJump(1, …)).

name: Reverse super
description: Dash along the ground, then hold the stick the other way and jump in the dash (press jump with the dash and flip the stick in the dash freeze). CheckForSuperJump sends the super's momentum the stick's way (MoveAxis.x), not the dash's: 805 up and 900 sideways (dashJumpMagnitude), backwards. The dash still carries the dot forward on its tick and the jump's (Velocity 1670 on the jump tick, 29 u forward in all), then the run speed turns from +460 to -460 over 7 ticks, so it matches a plain super the other way only 9 ticks after the dash, about 157 u behind it (Course 1 WJ_DS start: x 2004 vs 1847 at dash+15). With no sideways stick at the jump it is a plain super the dash's way.
note: The overlay's REVERSED SUPER: the stick points against the dash at the jump. Demo (Course 1 WJ_DS quick restart): 10 ticks standing, dash right with jump on dash-frame 1 and the stick left through the dash (lockX -1), then hold left. The 1x probe and the offline engine match tick for tick.

name: Reverse super on switching block
description: The dash's block swap turns the blue floor off under the dot; the jump on dash frame 1 is still a super because coyote keeps onGround. Dash right with the stick locked left (lockX -1) gives a reverse super: 805 up, 876 momentum left.

name: Super in switching blocks
description: The wall doesn't kill the dot because it stays in the wall too short.

name: Super in switching spikes
description: Actually the same as super in switching blocks.

name: Inwall super into wall
description: Clip in the wall like in the video, turn, do a super, turn back.

name: Inwall reverse super
description: Clip in the wall like in the video and do a reverse super.

name: Inwall super
description: Clip in the wall like in the video, then turn and turn again, and then do a super.

name: Edge spike jump next to wall
description: A spike grace jump off the edge of spikes next to a wall (like the one spike jump).
note: Demonstrated on the injected edge-spike-jump-wall lab map: out from under a low ceiling, a jump off the spike strip at a wall's foot on the grace's last tick, up the wall's face to its top.

name: Spike wallbounce
description: A wallbounce next to spikes: the dot dashes into the wall and jumps off it (the superbounce) and brushes the spikes for one tick, inside their grace (spike grace).
note: Demo cut from the 2_WJ_DS 1.68 route on Course 2 (around tick 165): the overlay marks the SUPERBOUNCE, then SPIKE GRACE two ticks later. Demonstrated on the injected spike-wallbounce lab map: a superbounce out of a plain window in a spiked wall face; the bounce's first tick brushes the spikes above for one tick (free Enter) and the bounce carries the dot clear. Replaces the Course 2 cut.

name: Edge spike jump
description: A spike grace jump off the edge of spikes (like the one spike jump).
note: Demonstrated on the injected edge-spike-jump lab map: run into a floor spike strip and jump on the 3rd tick (Enter, Stay 1, jump), 18 u past the last jump that never touches it, onto a platform that jump can't reach.

name: Spike super
description: A spike grace, like the one spike jump, but you do a super on the edge of the spikes.
note: Demonstrated on the injected spike-super lab map (moss floor, one dash): a ground dash enters the spike strip on its free Enter step and supers out on the next, one dash step (33 u) past the last super that avoids the strip; only such supers reach the platform.

name: Corner jump
description: There is a place on the edge of the spikes and the end of the platform where the dot can stay.
note: Demonstrated on the injected corner-jump lab map: the dot stands on the platform's end with 33 u of itself over a flush spike pit (only the back ground ray on the platform, the standing hurtbox 7 u above the spikes), waits, and a standing jump from there reaches a platform a tick-shorter stand can't.

name: Inwall wallbounce
description: Was kind of fixed, but: when you clip in a wall and do a wallbounce on the very bottom edge of the wall, the dot clips a bit into the wall and earns vertical momentum. The lift is a step-up in every rendered frame, so the steps are capped by FPS either way (1x tests from the bottom of Course 1's hanging wall, at 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 / 280 fps): with interpolation on, as the game ships, it climbed 0 / 0 / 57 / 57 / 113; with interpolation off, 57 / 113 / 169 / 225 / 337.
note: Lab: start in the pauselift-wall lab's cling on a wall whose top is at 600. Dash with the stick at rest and turnX -1: each turned dash lifts 112 (to y 207, then 318.8) and clings again. The jump 2 inputs after the second dash is the dash-boosted wallbounce (276, 730, momentum.y 400.8), onto the wall's top, finish on tick 38. Ghosts: `one-dash` (536.8, slides back down) and `no-turn` (dashes away from the wall).

name: Pauselift
description: An inwall wallbounce with the game paused in the turned dash's tick. Movement.Update's step-up runs outside the pause check, so every paused frame lifts the dot another 56 units, up to the top of the wall it is in.
note: Test-Pauselift (Course 4's left column, face x 19936, top 13001): the super off the floating block turns into the wall facing away, the dash with turnX lifts 6 times a tick unpaused; paused 40 frames after that dash's second tick it lifts 35 times, 11111.6 to the slab top at 13037, then a super and double jump peak at (20352.4, 13533.4). The demo holds the pause menu open at the apex. The overlay's PAUSELIFT: an inwall climb (a step-up with the forward rays against the facing) while the pause menu is open, once per pause. The route's pause (MacroStep.pauseFrames) plays at 1x and in turbo and the offline engine alike. It needs the dash to start flush with the hitbox's short side against the wall (within ~0.1 u), which the super's momentum gives.

name: Reverse super pauselift
description: A pauselift started flush with the back against the wall, so the pause lifts on every rendered frame of the lifting tick instead of only its last one. The step-up's down ray has to be inside the wall on the paused frame's blend; from a cling the turned dash starts 13 u out and only the tick's last frames get there (1 of 6 at 280 fps), while from flush every frame does (6 of 6 up to 0.2 u out, 4 at 1 u, 3 at 2 u, 2 at 4 u). Turning away from a wall in place leaves a 10-12 u gap (the hitbox reaches 25.5 u in front and 15.5 u behind), so the dot has to be carried back into the wall while it faces away: stand about 100 u out facing away, dash away with the stick held toward the wall through the dash and jump on it (a reverse super: its momentum goes toward the wall), then let go of the stick, so it keeps facing away while the momentum pins its back flush against the wall. Then, still in the air (the super gives the dash back), the usual pauselift: dash with the stick at rest, tilt toward the wall in the freeze, pause, hold the menu until the dot stops rising. The tilt back can't be dropped: only the freeze turn makes the dot face the wall on a dash tick after the first while its forward rays still point away (offline: none of 972 tilt-free input sets lifted).
note: Demo on the pauselift-wall lab map, its second demo (labmaps/pauselift-wall.reverse-super.demo.json, with its own start on the lab's floor): 24 input ticks (10 past the dash, so the playback runs through the climb), the pause on frame 2 of the lifting tick; offline every pause frame of that tick climbs the 2000 u wall.

name: Edge stop
description: When you clip in a wall and go backwards on the bottom edge, the dot loses all vertical momentum; probably something with coyote frames.
note: The list's own placeholder name ("it doesn't have a name").

name: Infinite mossy blocks stamina
description: When you do an inwall super into a wall, all of the dot's abilities return.

name: Gap stick
description: In a small gap the dot starts falling really slowly and pushing into the wall a bit.

name: Slope sliding
description: The dot slides down in the wall, so it can clip in a bit.

name: Checkpoint mid air jump
description: A respawn (Movement.respawn: a death, or a quick restart off a course) puts the dot 12 u under the last checkpoint it touched and sets onGround, but keeps coyoteFrames from before. Most checkpoints sit at standing height, so nothing changes. One that respawns the dot above its floor leaves it in the air with onGround still true, and it can ground-jump there for as many ticks as it had coyote frames left: 6 after a restart from the ground, none from the air (onGround drops on the first tick). The checkpoint at 13402, 3159 (active in the Courses 6-10 world, off any course) respawns the dot 64 u above the floor; a jump 5 ticks after the restart (the last of the 6) leaves from 58 u up with the full 805 and peaks 311 u above the floor instead of 258.
note: Lab: the respawn point is 76 u above the floor, like the checkpoint at 13402, 3159. Stand 5 ticks, quick restart (the dot respawns at y 97.5 with onGround held), then jump right on input 10, the last coyote tick: the 805 jump from y 89.9 peaks at 347.7 and lands on the ledge (top 290), finish on tick 42. Ghosts: `ground` (no restart: the jump peaks at 291.8, into the ledge's face) and `late` (no jump).

name: Checkpoint mid air super
description: Same as "Checkpoint mid air jump", but do a super.
note: Demo on the injected checkpoint-midair-super lab map (WJ_DS, offline). The lab starts in the state a respawn leaves 64 u above a floor: onGround held, coyoteFrames 5, falling. Dash right on the 4th tick with jump on dash frame 1: a super from y 92.6 that peaks at 347.5 (the same super from the floor peaks at 288.8, ghost `ground`). The `restart` demo does the whole thing with a real quick restart: the start sets respawnPoint 76 u above the floor, then reset on input 5 and the super on tick 10. The mined main demo starts after the respawn because the miner drops every window that contains a reset.

name: Checkpoint mid air walljump
description: A respawn (Movement.respawn: a quick restart, or a death) sets onGround and zeroes Velocity and momentum, but leaves the wall state alone: wallCoyoteFrames and wallJumpsLeft from a cling carry to the checkpoint. wallCoyoteFrames doesn't count down while the dot is on the ground (standing or walking), so the carried 7 waits there; after the next ground jump (or leaving a ledge) it counts down a tick at a time, and a jump press while it is still above 0 is a wall jump off no wall (getPlayerControlledInput: jumpBuffer && (OnWall || wallCoyoteFrames > 0), checked before the double jump): Velocity.y 730 and 460 sideways, away from the way the dot faces, spending a wall jump instead of the double jump. With a dash started 1-5 ticks before (dashBoostMin 0 < framesSinceLastDash < dashBoostMax 6) it is the superbounce's SpecialWallJump(0.6, 0.6, up*410): 730 up, 276 sideways, a 3-tick lock and 410 momentum up that decays only by the momentum Lerp (about 8 a tick).
note: Lab: jump right into the wall and cling (tick 24, wallCoyoteFrames 7), then quick restart on input 25 to the respawn point at standing height. Jump on input 28, then jump again with left on input 34 (wallCoyoteFrames 1): a wall jump off no wall, Velocity (-460, 730). It peaks 292 u above the floor (a jump: 258) and lands on the left ledge, finish on tick 66. Ghosts: `no-cling` and `late` (second press on input 36).

name: Up clip through slope and block
description: Jump facing the slope, turn and jump: the slope pushes the dot into the block so it can go through.

name: Fast steps slopes
description: The dot just steps up really fast many times.

name: Fast steps blocks
description: Same as "Fast steps slopes".

name: Fast steps blocks clip
description: A step is a teleport, so the dot steps and teleports up through anything.

name: Fast steps slopes glitch
description: The step teleports the dot a bit into the wall, and then jump spam doesn't kill the dot.

name: Inslope wallbounce
description: Clip into a slope and do a wallbounce.

name: Spike noclip respawn
description: If the dot respawns in spikes, they don't kill it: the player never leaves the spike on death (which usually happens when they respawn).

name: Spike fall
description: Spikes aren't a place the dot can stand on, so it starts falling and the hurtbox goes a bit lower.
note: Demonstrated on the injected spike-fall lab map: running across a flush spike patch the ground rays can't stand on; the dot falls into it for one tick and the step-up lifts it onto the far floor inside the grace (up to 100 u wide at full speed).

name: Roof squeeze
description: Spam jump for the short hitbox, so the dot can squeeze through a gap.

name: Squeeze clip
description: In a small space the dot can be pushed through thin walls.

name: Dash mid air coyote jump
description: Dash flat off a ledge and jump after the dash. The dash doesn't fall (its Velocity.y is 0, and its end sets it to 10), and coyote time (maxCoyoteFrames 6) only starts counting on the first tick the ground rays miss. So a dash that leaves the ledge late in its 11 ticks still has coyote ticks left when it ends, and a jump then is a full ground jump in mid air: 805 up, about 120 u past the last tick on the ground. Pressed inside the dash in the same window, the jump is a super instead (CheckForSuperJump runs while onGround lasts).
note: Lab: walk right 8 ticks from x -300 and dash right. The dash's last 3 ticks are past the ledge, and coyote time only counts from the first tick the ground rays miss. Jump on input 11 (coyoteFrames 2): the full 805 ground jump from x 131.9 in mid air, onto the far block, finish on tick 81. Ghosts: `no-dash` (the latest running coyote jump) and `late` (a tick after the coyote ran out) both land in the pit.

name: Momentum after quick restart
description: Not momentum itself: respawn(true) zeroes Velocity, momentum and movingPlatformVelocity, but leaves state behind that gives speed back at the checkpoint. 1) The wall jump's lock (wallJumpMovementLockRemaining, wallJumpDirection): a restart within 5 ticks of a wall jump runs at a full 460 (MoveLeftAndRight's locked Velocity.x) from the checkpoint's first tick, with no acceleration. 2) A zip mover's history (platformMomentumHistory, movingPlatformCoyote): a restart within 7 ticks of leaving one, then a jump, adds the mover's fastest recent velocity as momentum (MovingPlatformMomentumInherit). 3) The ground bounce's window (DashBounceFrames, omnidash): a jump in the 4 ticks after the restart adds the bounce's momentum up. Coyote, wall coyote and the jump buffer carry too (checkpoint mid air jump).
note: Lab (the wall jump's lock): cling on the left wall, wall jump right on input 25, quick restart on input 26. The lock carries through the respawn, so Velocity.x is 460 on the respawn's own tick with no acceleration. The jump on input 27 clears the pit onto the block's edge (x 579.4), finish on tick 89. Ghosts: `no-walljump` (restart from the cling) and `late` (restart 7 ticks after the wall jump) both ramp up from 0, come down 25 u short and die. A restart up to 6 ticks after the wall jump still carries the lock, 7 doesn't. The zip mover and ground bounce cases have no lab.

name: Ultra
description: A hyper 4 units lower: a hyper whose jump is at least 4 u below the last hyper's (or ground stay's) height (lastHyperY), with the dash going the way the dot already moved, also gets back the momentum from before the dash (preDashMomentum.x) on top of the hyper's.
note: Lab: the ultra lab's hyper chain, with the second hyper jumping 50 u under lastHyperY (the rule is 4 u). CheckForSuperJump adds preDashMomentum.x (635.5): momentum 2230.7, finish on tick 80. The `level` ghost runs the same inputs with both hypers on the upper floor: a plain hyper's 1609.4.

name: GC Wall Clip
description: Game-controller wall clip. Rising with your back to a wall (the hitbox's back edge within ~8 units of it), flick the stick lightly toward the wall and back. The hitbox is offset 5 units to the front (collider offset x 5, width 41), so the turn swings its back edge 10 units into the wall; the depenetration pushes it only part way out, and the next tick the front ground ray (x-25) starts inside the wall and grounds you in mid air if vertical speed is under 200. A buffered jump then is a full ground jump, and the grounding refills air dashes, double jumps and wall jumps on a Ground-tagged wall (touchedSolidGround). The light flick back leaves you within 8 units of the wall, facing away from it, so you can clip the same wall again (Course 1 NONE does it twice per face). Cut clip: hold the jump from the last clip, release it on the flick tick (Velocity.y between 150 and 580 is cut to 50) and press it on the flick-back tick: the next clip comes 10 ticks after the last instead of waiting for Velocity.y under 200. A clip also works falling (Velocity.y is under 200), as long as the ground rays' height (y-18) is inside the wall. A third clip off the same face doesn't happen: every stick value 0.3-1 on the second flick and flick back leaves the back edge 9.4 units or more out. Needs no unlock.
note: The offline solver grafts it: a WallBehind contact (in the air, not dashing, Velocity.y under 580, a wall within 12 units of x∓15 at y-18) gets the flick with the jump released, the jump pressed with the flick back, then a hold (OfflineSolver.WallClip).

name: KB Wall Clip
description: Keyboard wall clip: GC Wall Clip with full-tilt inputs. Rising with your back within ~8 units of a wall and vertical speed under 200, press toward the wall for 1-3 ticks, with jump pressed up to 0.12 s before, on that tick or on the next: the turn clips the hitbox into the wall and the jump is a full ground jump. Turning back at full tilt leaves you ~0.6 units further out than a light flick (8.3 units from the wall after the Course 1 NONE clip), past the 8-unit limit, so clipping the same wall again needs another way back in. Offline on Course 1 NONE, a tap on any tick from 43 to 59 clips. Needs no unlock.

name: Late gate touch
description: A flying start from behind the start gate. The timer starts when the player first overlaps the start gate (startGate.OnTriggerStay calls courseScript.startTracking, which does nothing while the timer runs), and an end gate before the timer runs does nothing either (stopTracking only acts while tracking). So a route can reach the far side of the gate untimed, through the end gates, and touch the gate for a tick at the last moment on its way into the course. Course 1 NONE 1.40: GC wall clips up the pillar's left face and the shelf's left edge before the timer (End (1) and RealEnd do nothing yet), over the pillar and down its right face onto the end of the floor (x 2544.8, facing left, just clear of the gate's right edge at 2518), a jump, a tap left on the jump's 14th tick (the hitbox's left edge over the gate, the head still under the pillar) to start the timer, and the first right-face clip 8 ticks later, where the old route touched the gate 20 ticks before it: 1.62 to 1.40. The farm time grows (4.20 s from the restart); the record counts only the timer.

name: Coyote jump
description: A ground jump after the ground rays stopped hitting (coyoteFrames < maxCoyoteFrames). Demonstrated on the injected coyote-ledge lab map: run right off the ledge; gap A is only crossed by a coyote jump (any coyote tick), gap B only by the last coyote tick, jump held for the full height.

name: Wall coyote jump
description: A wall jump after the wall rays stopped hitting. The cling branch sets OnWall and wallCoyoteFrames = maxWallCoyoteFrames (7) every tick the rays hit; once they miss, a branch of its own counts wallCoyoteFrames down with OnWall still on, and getPlayerControlledInput's wall jump (jumpBuffer && (OnWall || wallCoyoteFrames > 0)) fires on any of the 8 ticks after the last cling tick: the count reaches 0 on the 7th, and OnWall outlives it by one tick because only the next tick's else branch clears it. The jump is the plain one, (460, 730) with the 7-tick lock, and always away from the wall: while OnWall is on, the animator block sets localScale.x to wallCoyoteDir each tick, and the wall jump goes against localScale. Three more things hold through the window: the fall keeps the wall slide's physics (ApplyWallslideFriction(0.7) pulls Velocity.y toward the slide speed and the fast fall is off, so a slide off a wall's bottom at -382 slows to -327 instead of speeding up), the stick moves the dot freely (it can drift under the wall it left), and a dash does not flip away from the wall (the flip needs wallCoyoteFrames == maxWallCoyoteFrames: from a full cling a neutral dash goes away from the wall, a tick into the coyote window it goes the way the dot faces, under the wall).
note: Demonstrated on the injected wall-coyote-window lab map (WJ): slide off a hanging wall's bottom, hold right and jump on the 7th coyote tick, through a window in a spike wall 75 u to the right. Every wall jump rises 14.6 u for every 9.2 u across under the lock, so near the wall a wall jump off the wall itself (from y 186 or higher) is still too high for the window, and a jump cut only comes 6 ticks in; a fall through the window cannot rise to the finish box. Offline every press tick off the wall dies at the window; the 5th-8th coyote tick finishes (the 7th and 8th clear of the spikes).

name: Stored wall jump
description: A wall jump off no wall, anywhere, from a wall coyote count carried over the ground. The ground branch sets OnWall off but never touches wallCoyoteFrames, and only the air (else) branch and the wall coyote branch count it down, so a landing straight from a cling (a slide down to the floor: 7 left) or inside the wall coyote window keeps what is left for as long as the dot stays on the ground, however far it walks. The count starts falling on the first tick in the air (a ground jump, or walking off a ledge, where the ground coyote jump still comes first), and a jump press on the 2nd-7th tick after the ground jump (the 1st needs the button up again) takes getPlayerControlledInput's wall jump branch, which it checks before the double jump: Velocity.y 730 and 460 away from the way the dot faces (the jump goes against localScale; running right it kicks left), with the 7-tick lock, spending a wall jump that the next landing refills. On the last tick it adds 59 u to a ground jump (390.8 against 331.8 above the floor). With the double jump it comes first, so the double jump is kept: ground jump, stored wall jump, double jump (621 against 578 for a ground and double jump). A new cling resets the count to 7; a wall jump, a dash from a full cling or 7 ticks in the air use it up. Quick restarts and deaths carry it too (checkpoint-midair-walljump).
note: Demonstrated on the injected stored-walljump lab map (WJ): cling to a post, slide onto the floor, run 300 u right, jump and press again 6 ticks later with no wall in reach; the finish box is out of reach of every ground jump (the floor's and the post top's) and of every wall jump off the post. The overlay's STORED WALL JUMP: a wall jump with OnWall off and wallCoyoteFrames above 0 on its input.

name: Stored superbounce
description: The stored wall jump as the dash boost. getPlayerControlledInput makes a wall jump within dashBoostMax (6) frames of a dash the superbounce's SpecialWallJump(0.6, 0.6, up * dashBoostUpwards): Velocity (276 away from the facing, 730) and 410 momentum up. A super ends its dash, so with a stored count (a landing from a cling), a super on the floor and a jump press 2-4 ticks later is that boost off no wall, while the super's 900 momentum keeps the dot going: 537 above the floor at the peak, against 329 for the super alone and 391 for the stored wall jump alone.
note: Demonstrated on the injected stored-superbounce lab map (WJ_DS): slide off a post onto the floor, super right on the landing tick (jump on dash frame 2), press jump again 3 ticks after the dash. The checkpoint route's version (checkpoint-midair-walljump) is the same boost from a count a quick restart carried. The overlay marks the SUPERBOUNCE and STORED WALL JUMP on the same tick.

name: Backwards dash-jump
description: Standing against a wall, turn away from it and press dash and jump on the same tick. The dash start moves the dot 20 u against the dash, back into the wall, and the buffered jump is a grounded dash jump from inside it.
note: Demo on the injected backwards-dash-jump lab map (WJ_DS, offline): walk right into a wall (the dot stops at x 274.5), then stick left, jump and dash on the same tick. The dash starts with the wall behind it and the jump is the grounded dash jump (super: 805 up, 876 momentum left). Finish box on tick 32. In the offline engine the -20 shove into the wall makes no difference to the super's path: a no-wall control has the identical trajectory.

name: Superbounce
description: Dash into a wall with the jump buffered within dashBoostMax (6) frames of the dash: the airborne wall touch ends the dash and the game's dash boost, SpecialWallJump(0.6, …), bounces up on Velocity.y 730 plus 410 up momentum (the touch must land inside those 6 frames and after the buffer, so a press a full tick later misses it). Demonstrated on the injected superbounce-wall lab map (a plain wall in empty space), solved at WJ_DS.

name: Superbounce double jump
description: Dash flat into a wall with jump pressed with the dash, so the jump is buffered when the dash reaches the wall inside the dash boost window: the superbounce, SpecialWallJump(0.6, 1, up*410), Velocity.y 730 plus 410 momentum up. Double jump 1 or 2 ticks after the bounce: after a jump that wasn't a normal one the air jump only needs Velocity.y < 700, and it keeps half the speed it finds (Velocity.y = airJumpForce + v/2, 745 + 649/2 = 1069.5 two ticks after; 1083 one tick after), while the bounce's ~383 momentum still pushes up, so the dot rises at about 1450 u/s. A double jump on the bounce tick (730, over the gate) doesn't fire. The stick doesn't change the climb: neutral, up and toward the wall give the same speeds. Holding down (fast fall) costs 10.8 u/s: the dash leaves the body's vertical speed at 0, under the fast fall's 300 limit, so the bounce tick's gravity is 1.4x (692.2 after it instead of 703). With the stick neutral the bounce's 276 u/s sideways speed dies in 3 ticks; the dot drifts ~37 u off the wall and goes straight up into the roof. Demo (Course 1 WJ_DS_DJ): from the platform at 3028, -245, super left, flick the stick right for 1 tick, then hold down; dash with jump into the hanging wall's right face at 2553.5, -50; double jump; bonk the roof at y 494 (the roof is at 521); dash left over the wall to the finish.
note: Lab: jump right, dash right into the wall on input 6 with the jump on dash frame 1. The superbounce comes on the dash's 3rd frame (momentum.y 400.8). Double jump 2 ticks later: 745 + 649/2 = 1069.5. It climbs about 29 u a tick into the box high on the wall (finish tick 30, peak 779.7). Ghosts: `no-double` (437.3) and `jump-double` (375). No fast fall is held.

name: Hyper
description: Omnidash (Vman): diagonal-down dash and jump. The landing turns the dash flat (canHyper) and the jump in it is the hyper (CheckForSuperJump's hyper branch): 547 up (805 x 0.68) and 1650 sideways momentum (hyperJumpMagnitude).
note: Also called wavedash. The overlay's HYPER.

name: Chained hyper
description: Omnidash (Vman): two hypers chained; the second dash starts in the air of the first one's jump.
note: It is an Ultra when the second hyper jumps at least 4 u lower than the first (Ultra). The overlay's CHAINED HYPER.

name: Float Ultra
description: Omnidash (Vman): an ultra (a chained hyper whose second jump is at least 4 u under the first's, so the game adds back the pre-dash momentum) that gets its drop from FloatingOrigin instead of the floor. FloatingOrigin keeps the player within Threshold (17500 in the Vman world, Use2DDistance off) of scene (0, 0): the frame after the player leaves that sphere, it moves every root object back by the player's scene position, so the dot is near scene (0, 0) again. lastHyperY, which the first hyper writes, is a scene-frame height the rebase leaves alone, so if the sphere is crossed between the two hypers (no ground stay in between rewrites lastHyperY), the second hyper is ~11,700 u 'lower' in the scene frame on the same floor and the check passes.
note: VMAN: the platform above and left of Course 4 (floor y 11625, x 12100-13300) is where the first sphere's edge crosses. Demo: a fresh VMAN game, the run's best fast-forwarded in turbo to its quick restart on that platform (input 635), then at 1x: 26 ticks walking right, hop, wavedash right (jump on dash frame 4), a second wavedash 14 input ticks later (jump on dash frame 6). The first hyper at world (12845, 11663) writes lastHyperY 11663; the dot leaves the sphere in its air at scene (13030, 11704) and the next tick the world moves by (-13030, -11704); the second hyper at world (13687, 11665), 2 u higher, is at scene y -38 < 11663 - 4: Did an ultra!, momentum 1609 + 1131 = 2740. Then the demo goes back down the way the run came up to the left end of Course 1's floor, 17,500 from the platform, and the world moves again by (12794, 11947) (found by fulltas; turbo and the offline engine rebase as 1x does, and tools/tech-check.py replays the demo's turbo trace offline with the ultra at the same tick). The run's best as saved does its first ultra on the same platform (jump at x 13041, tick 1169) by height: 11661 under 11666.6 - 4, with origin (0, 0); it leaves the sphere at x 13133 the next tick, after the ultra. The overlay's FLOAT ULTRA; the demo draws the sphere, coordinates, the ultra line and a world minimap of every sphere it was in. Also demonstrated on the float-ultra lab map (start-c1-none's FloatingOrigin: currentOrigin (-2241, 304), Threshold 17500). A floor at world y 17000 crosses the sphere at world x 4853. The VMAN demo's inputs (walk 26, hop, wavedash with jump on dash frame 4, second wavedash 14 ticks later with jump on dash frame 6) get the ultra (momentum 1609.4 + 1130.7 = 2740.1), which clears a 1200 u gap to the finish box on tick 103. The same lab 2000 u lower (inside the sphere) gives a plain hyper (1609.4) that falls short. In game it ultras only when the origin is (-2241, 304).

name: Ground bounce
description: Omnidash (Vman): dash straight down into the ground and jump in the dash. The landing ends the dash with DashBounceFrames, and the jump adds dashBounceMagnitude: 805 + 600 = 1390 up.
note: Also called dash bounce.

name: Hyper ground bounce
description: WJ DS DJ + omnidash: diagonal down dash, jump (hyper), then dash straight down into the ground and jump (ground bounce). You keep the momentum of both: the down dash puts 95 % of the hyper's sideways momentum back when it lands (endDash, preDashMomentum.x), so the bounce leaves at 1390 up and ~1840 sideways (a ground bounce alone: 0).
note: Offline (clip lab, VMAN floor, running at 460): hyper, down dash in its air, jump on the down dash's first frame.

name: Super ground bounce
description: Hyper ground bounce with a super instead of the hyper: super, then dash straight down into the ground and jump. A bit less sideways speed: the bounce leaves with 1390 up and ~870 sideways momentum (a hyper's gives ~1740), plus the stick's run speed.
note: Lab: the super on input 0 (dash right, jump on dash frame 1), then on input 12 a straight-down dash with the jump on dash frame 2. endDash gives back 95 % of the super's momentum, so the ground bounce leaves at (868.8, 586.6), finish on tick 49. A down dash pressed during the dash cooldown waits and then goes the way the dot faces, so it has to come on input 12 or later. Ghosts: `hyper` (the wave bounce, 1736.7) and `jump` (0 sideways).

name: Wall dash
description: Omnidash (Vman): a dash from a wall cling goes away from the wall with x set to ±1 after the normalize, so a diagonal one moves at (1670, 1181) u/s. Down-diagonal onto a floor, it becomes a wavedash off the wall.

name: Spring dash
description: A dash that cancels a sideways spring's lock.
note: Demonstrated on the injected spring-dash lab map (WJ_DS, offline): walk into a sideways spring (the Course 5 ceiling spring's SpringScript) under a spike ceiling with a dash armed for the lock's first tick (springDash 1, lockX 1). The dash ends the spring cutscene and runs level at y 49.2 under the spikes (ticks 19-29) to the finish on tick 88; the locked launch rises into the ceiling and dies on tick 24. The spring's cancelSpringCutscene (movementLock 0.25 s) still fires mid-dash and sets cutsceneMode none, so the dash's natural end gives back none of the stored 4689 momentum.x; only a hit that ends the dash earlier keeps it (spring-dash-stack).

name: Spike grace
description: Inside a spike for the ticks its graceFrames allow without dying (a spike kills once its contact count passes graceFrames). One spike jump is the classic use: 1) grace frames; 2) the single spike isn't blocking one of your ground colliders; 3) the ground detectors extend down further than your hurtbox (thanks varii for the description).
note: Demo (from the tech_one_spike_jump recording): fall onto the single spike on the platform right of Course 1's hanging wall with jump pressed two ticks before landing; the buffered jump leaves on the landing tick, inside the spike's grace, and it repeats. The overlay marks each landing as SPIKE GRACE. Demonstrated on the injected spike-grace lab map (a shaft with one spike): the fall touches the spike on ticks 17-18 (Enter free, Stay counts 1) and the buffered jump leaves on the landing tick 19, before the 2nd Stay. The 'late' ghost jumps a tick later and dies.

name: Pixel perfect corner boost
description: A chained diagonal dash boost that double counts momentum and sends you flying; only on corners (a maybe-pixel-perfect hyper off a corner).
note: Demo on the injected corner-boost lab map (offline): ledges stepping down. First a hyper off ledge 1's corner: the flat dash slides off the edge with onGround held and jumps on dash frame 6. Late in its fall, a second down-right dash lands on ledge 2 and slides off its edge, and the jump pressed after the landing gives the second corner hyper, 100 u lower. The game's ultra check adds preDashMomentum.x (548.8) to the 1650: 2146 after the tick, against 1609 for a plain hyper. Nothing counts the momentum twice beyond that Ultra bonus, so this is the Ultra bonus chained down ledges. A jump buffered before the landing (it fires at framesSinceLastDash 4) gets the pre-dash momentum but not the 1650: 1217.8 in a shorter layout of the lab.

name: Freeze aim
description: Omnidash: press dash with the stick at rest, then in the dash freeze push the stick straight up (or down) with a slight lean, sideways 0.3-0.4 (e.g. 0.35, 1). Movement.Update turns the waiting dash to that stick without the snap a pressed dash gets (getPlayerControlledInput drops x when |x| < 1 and y is full), so the dash goes 19° off vertical: dashDirection (0.33, 0.944), 552 u/s sideways and 1576 u/s up. No dash pressed on a tick has that angle; the 8 ways are straight up (1670 up) or the diagonal (1181 each way).
note: Needs an analog stick (a keyboard or d-pad can't give 0.3-0.4); the timing is the dash turn's: any frame of the freeze, the last one before the next tick counting. The dash's first tick still goes the way the player faces (the -20 shove and that tick's Velocity come before the freeze). From standing on Course 1's floor it peaks 268 u up and 124 u across with the stick at rest after it; a straight-up dash peaks 298 u up. Down in the air it still lands as a wavedash. The overlay's FREEZE AIM: a dash steeper than the diagonal on its first dash tick (0 < |x| < 0.7, y != 0). Routes give it as the dash tick's turnX/turnY (MacroStep.dashTurnX/dashTurnY); the solver tries it as the omnidash kind steep. Demo on the injected freeze-aim lab map (WJ_DS_DJ_BS_ORB_ZIP_OM): from a ledge under a ceiling, dash with the stick at rest and turn to (0.35, 1) in the freeze; the dash leans out past the ceiling's end, over a spike bed, and drops onto a spiked pillar's top (the finish box, tick 29). The lab's three keyboard ghosts don't land: up-right (the spike bed), up in the freeze then right (straight up into the ceiling, then the spiked face), and the closest of 3,556 keyboard dash tries, walk left 9 ticks then up-right (the spiked face 37 u below the top). Hand play shows all four ghosts, each in its own lane (a see-through copy of the lab), the keyboard ones marked KB; the demo's playback runs the three keyboard ones beside the player; the studio's lab preview draws all four paths. docs/human-input.md.

name: Zip mover intangibility
description: Jump or wall-jump while touching a zip mover (PlatformMover, locked or not): Movement.MovingPlatformMomentumInherit calls PlatformMover.MakeIntangible, which moves the block from the Ground layer to Default for WaitForSeconds(0.15). For those 8 physics ticks the ground and wall rays (Ground only) miss it and the normal hitbox (it excludes Default) passes into it; only the smaller 40x54 hurtbox still collides. The mover needn't be touched: within movingPlatformCoyote (7 ticks after leaving it, on the ground or a wall), any jump, super or wall jump off anything calls lastTouchedMovingPlatform.MakeIntangible (Movement.cs 1516-1518). A dash along its face in that window doesn't stop on it as a wall: it runs on until the block is Ground again (from the 8th tick after the jump), then clings.
note: Lab on Course 5 overgrown's zip mover (Course 15's world): walk left into its right face, jump while touching it (MakeIntangible, 0.15 s), dash left 3 inputs later. The dash runs 5 ticks against the face and clings on the 8th tick after the jump; the zip then carries the cling into the box (tick 50). The `no-touch` ghost jumps just before the touch and clings on the dash's first tick.

name: Boosted double jump
description: The double jump's gate (getPlayerControlledInput, Movement.cs 1763) is Velocity.y < 200 after a normal jump but Velocity.y < 700 after any other: a hyper (1432), a ground bounce jump (1704), a spring (hitSpring 2466), an up dash's end (endDash 2016-2018), a wall kick (SpecialWallJump 1564). It sets Velocity.y = 745 + max(v, 0) / 2 (1769-1774), so a double jump early after one of those keeps half its speed: one tick after a hyper (520 after gravity) it is 1005 up with the hyper's 1650 momentum still carrying; four ticks after a ground bounce (697) it is 1093 on top of its ~550 momentum up. The superbounce's case is the superbounce double jump.
note: Demonstrated on the injected boosted-double-jump lab map (WJ_DS_DJ_BS_ORB_ZIP_OM, offline): from standing on a moss floor, jump, dash down-right, hyper on dash frame 4 (tick 8), double jump on the next tick (Velocity.y 520 -> 1005, momentum 1570) over a spiked pillar face into the box over its top on tick 20. Only a hyper reaches the box's edge by tick 20 (a super is at x 785 at most), and from the hyper to tick 20 Velocity.y stays at 200 or more, so any double jump there is the boosted one: the bare hyper arc dies on the spikes, and the fastest run without it found (a super) arrives on tick 26. After the hyper an exhaustive lab solve --forbid-boosted-double-jump (--from-inputs 2 --max-ticks 20 --exact) proves it: all 308 distinct states on tick 9 are cut by the free-flight bound (the collider's top reaches y 190.7 at most by tick 20, the box starts at 210). At 1x (tools/probe.py --tech) it plays as offline: HYPER, then BOOSTED DOUBLE JUMP at Velocity.y 1005.2, over the face into the box. The overlay's BOOSTED DOUBLE JUMP: a double jump that finds Velocity.y at 200 or more (only the 700 gate lets it through).

name: Final-cling float
description: A cling on a mossy wall with no wall jumps left calls outOfWallJumpsCling (Movement.cs 1061-1064, 1921-1931): isFinalWallClingActive on, finalWallClingTimeLeft 0.7 s, Velocity.y 0. While the flag is on, gravity is skipped (1109-1124) unless the dot falls faster than 75 u/s off ground and wall, and the flag is cleared only by the air branch with wallJumpsLeft < 0 (1080-1083) or the timer. A refill of wallJumpsLeft while it is on (a Ground-tagged floor or wall: touchedSolidGround 2162, a spring 2473, a refresh orb) leaves it stuck, so the next jump rises at its launch speed with no gravity until the rest of the 0.7 s is spent: a ground jump holds 805 u/s for up to ~33 ticks. Ways in: cling on the mossy wall with 0 wall jumps then quick-restart onto a checkpoint on Ground floor (respawn keeps the flag and OnWall), or reach a metal wall, floor, spring or orb within the 7 wall coyote ticks. With the double jump, a double jump inside the final cling's wall coyote ticks should float the same way (the air branch that clears the flag doesn't run there; read from the code, not probed).
note: Demonstrated on the injected final-cling-float lab map (WJ): a chimney with a mossy wall (x 80-120) and a metal one (x 172-212) 52 u apart. The dot starts in the air against the moss with no wall jumps left: that cling is the final one (the flag on, Velocity.y 0, 0.7 s). Turning right puts the metal wall under the front ground ray, which grounds the dot in mid-air (as a GC wall clip does) and refills the wall jumps with the flag still on; the ground jump pressed next holds 805 up with no gravity until physics tick 35 (0.7 s after the cling), then arcs: peak 851.8, into the finish box at tick 37. Offline control: the same inputs starting with 4 wall jumps left (no final cling) peak at 556. The overlay's FINAL-CLING FLOAT: a jump with isFinalWallClingActive still on. At 1x (tools/probe.py --tech) it plays as offline: FINAL-CLING FLOAT, into the box.

name: Ground bounce momentum pump
description: Chained ground bounces grow sideways momentum. A straight-down dash that lands runs endDash in the dash (1165-1171), which gives back 95% of preDashMomentum.x whatever its sign (2030-2033) and sets DashBounceFrames 4; the bounce jump then adds momentum.x * 0.05 * 10 (addMomentum((1, 0), momentum.x * 0.05), 1700-1704): x1.5. Ground friction is skipped while DashBounceFrames > 0 (2195-2199). Each cycle (bounce jump, down dash after the 0.18 s cooldown, land, buffered bounce) multiplies the momentum by 0.95 x 1.5 before ~10 ticks of decay: about +14% a cycle, at the same height. Hold the stick with the momentum or at rest (against it costs 25 a tick).
note: Measured on the injected ground-bounce-pump lab map (metal floor, offline): a hyper, then five ground bounces, each a straight-down dash 9 input ticks after the last jump with jump on dash frame 2 and the stick at rest. Momentum.x right after each bounce: 1736.7, 1927.0, 2143.5, 2390.1, 2670.8 (ticks 22/40/58/76/94), about +11 % a cycle at the same height. With the first bounce and no more dashes it is down to 124 by tick 104 (ghost `once`).

name: Dash momentum storage
description: A dash moves momentum into preDashMomentum (1643-1644) and its natural end (1143, cutsceneMode still dash) gives 95% back when the sign matches and the dash wasn't up (2028-2034); ground friction (x0.75 a tick on metal, x0.85 on mossy) never touches it in between. A jump on the dash's end tick is a normal 805 jump with the 95% kept, where a super (CheckForSuperJump never calls endDash, 1406) or a dash into a wall (the cling ends the cutscene first, 1038-1050) loses the stored momentum for good. Worth it over a super when 0.95 x the stored momentum is above the super's 900 (after a spring, a zip mover, a hyper or a wallbounce).
note: Demonstrated on the injected dash-momentum-storage lab map (WJ_DS, offline): landing with momentum.x 1448.2, a dash on the landing tick holds it through 11 ground ticks. The natural end (tick 23) gives back 1375.5, and a jump on that tick (the input after the dash's; dash ticks consume no input) lands on a platform past a spike pit (x 1916 at y -268, finish on tick 77). A super off the same dash (jump on its 10th frame) reaches x 1577 at best and a landing-tick jump with no dash x 1618; both die in the pit. A spring dash loses the storage if the spring's movementLock runs out mid-dash (see spring-dash).

name: Hyper stored superbounce
description: The stored superbounce off a hyper. The hyper's landing sets framesSinceLastDash 0 (1176) and the hyper fires from framesSinceLastDash 4 (1401); with a stored wall coyote count (a landing from a cling), a jump press on the next tick (5, inside dashBoostMax 6) takes the wall jump branch's boost, SpecialWallJump(0.6, 0.6, up * 410) (1712-1715), which adds to momentum: 730 Velocity up and 410 momentum up on top of the hyper's 1650 sideways.
note: Measured on the injected hyper-stored-superbounce lab map (offline; the stored-superbounce lab's post and floor with the omnidash). Cling down onto the floor, hop, then dash down-right with jump on dash frame 4: the hyper on tick 19. Jump again on the next tick (framesSinceLastDash 5): the dash boost off the stored count, Velocity (-276, 730) + 401 momentum up on top of the 1570 right. It peaks at y 489. One tick later (dash frame 5, the press at framesSinceLastDash 6) it is a plain stored wall jump that peaks at 300 (ghost `late`), so the window is one tick. The hyper alone peaks at 200 (ghost `hyper-only`).

name: Landing tick jump
description: Ground friction on momentum runs only on ground ticks where onGround was already on (touchedSolidGround 2193-2199: x0.75 on metal; touchedMossyGround 2264-2270: x0.85 on mossy), so a jump on the landing tick keeps all the momentum and one a tick later keeps 75% (85% on mossy). The same branch rewrites lastHyperY, so a landing-tick jump also leaves it alone.
note: Demonstrated on the injected landing-tick-jump lab map (NONE, offline): the dot starts in the air with momentum.x 2000 and the stick right. A jump pressed 4 ticks before the landing (buffered) leaves on the landing tick 12 with momentum.x 1448.2 kept and lands on a platform past a spike pit (x 1528 at y -268; finish on tick 60). The same jump a tick after the landing has 1058 (x0.75 friction), falls 130 u short, hits the platform's side and dies in the spikes. The overlay has no detector (a buffered jump on landing is most jumps).

name: Spring clip
description: A downward spring's momentum carries the dot through a spike strip a plain fall dies in. A spike kills on its 2nd OnTriggerStay2D (counter > graceFrames 1, spikeScript) and the first overlapping tick is OnTriggerEnter2D, so the dot may overlap it on 2 ticks and must be clear on the 3rd: through a 32-tall strip the hurtbox (40x54) has to travel 86 u in 3 ticks (28.7 u a tick). A plain fall tops out at 26.3 (fast-fall gravity 49.14 a tick, the drag toward -1120: -1316.6 u/s), 79.0 in 3. A spring pointing down (transform.up (0, -1)) calls hitSpring with no cutscene: 10 u down, momentum.y +upForce/4*10 - strength/4*10 and Velocity.y upForce*9 - strength*3 (hitSpring 2474-2477); the Course 5 ceiling spring (upForce 70, strength 300) gives momentum.y -575 and Velocity.y -270. The momentum decays 2.22% and 0.08 a tick while fast-fall gravity builds Velocity.y, and the body moves at Velocity + momentum, so for about 14-67 ticks after the hit (315-1933 u of drop) 3 ticks cover more than 86 u, 96 at best around tick 23. A floor, ceiling or wall contact on the way (a (0, ±1) normal, a cling) zeroes momentum.y and ends it.
note: Demonstrated on the injected spring-clip lab map (NONE, offline): jump right from a ledge into the downward spring hanging from a ceiling (the Course 5 spring's SpringScript) and hold down: the hit on tick 18 (Velocity.y -270, momentum.y -575), then 32.1 u a tick at the strip 618 u below, 96.3 over 3 ticks; the hurtbox is in the spikes on ticks 42 and 43 only (Enter, then Stay with counter 1) and lands in the finish box under them. The same jump mirrored away from the spring falls at a plain fall's 26.2 u a tick and dies on its 3rd tick in the strip. The crossing needs the right phase (a 10 u window of strip heights for one fall) and down held by the 2nd tick after the hit. The overlay marks the crossing as SPIKE GRACE.

name: Overhang slide
description: Moving sideways into an overhang (a surface whose normal points down and against the motion), Box2D's contact takes the into-surface part out of the body's velocity and leaves the along-surface part, which points down: (vx - vy)/2 down per second on a 45° overhang. Movement.FixedUpdate rewrites body.linearVelocity = Velocity + momentum every tick (1303), so the conversion holds on every contact tick, and momentum.x is left alone (OnCollisionStay2D zeroes momentum.y only on exact (0, ±1) normals, 2516-2531). A flat dash (1670) slides 16.7 u a tick down, momentum.x 1500 19.3 and 3000 33.6 (1680 u/s, over a plain fall's 26.3 terminal and the 28.67 a 32-tall spike strip needs); a sideways spring's launch (Course 5's Spring (2): momentum (3520, 125), Velocity.y 450) slides 24-27.6 a tick down from its first contact tick. Leaving the slope the extra speed isn't kept: Velocity.y still has the ordinary fall. In the normal world two exposed overhangs have room for the dot under them: (7255, 587)-(7856, 1188), 45°, facing down-right (move left into it), and (24278, -4285)-(25274, -5667), about 54° from vertical, facing down-left (move right into it).
note: Demonstrated on the injected overhang-slide lab map (NONE, offline): walk right into a sideways spring (the Course 5 Spring (2)'s SpringScript) whose launch meets a 1000x1000 box turned 45°: first contact on tick 25, then 24.1-27.6 u a tick down on ticks 26-42 (y 94.1 to -350.5, 444.6 u in 18 ticks) and into the finish band (y -600 to -400) on tick 50. The same launch the other way, with no overhang, rises for 21 ticks (it is 519 u higher on tick 42) and reaches the band on tick 85. Checked in a lab anchored at the real overhang at (7255, 587): momentum.x -3000 slides 33.6 a tick down.

name: Spring double hit
description: A down spring hit (hitSpring with up (0, -1): Velocity.y upForce*9 - strength*3, momentum.y +upForce/4*10 - strength/4*10, 2474-2477; the Course 5 ceiling spring: -270 and -575) refills the air jumps (2472). A double jump 2 ticks after it sets Velocity.y to airJumpForce, 745 (1768-1774), against about -550 momentum.y: the dot hovers a few u a tick inside the spring's 80x80 trigger until SpringScript's 0.15 s cooldown ends (OnTriggerStay2D: cooldown, Invoke endCooldown 0.15 s), and the spring hits again: momentum.y -1054.9, the double jump refilled. 3 or 4 ticks after the hit is too late (the dot has sunk out of the trigger), and a third hit fails (745 against about -1030 sinks out). Works for a spring pointing any way: sideways, a wall in front of the spring holds the dot in its trigger (nothing the player does counters a sideways push, and the stick is locked in the spring cutscene), and the second hit stacks momentum.x (4800 to 8781.3 with the Course 5 ceiling spring's SpringScript). The main demo is the downward case; the spring-double-hit-side lab is the sideways one.
note: Demonstrated on the injected spring-double-hit lab map (WJ_DS_DJ, offline), spring-clip's ledge and ceiling spring with a 32-tall spike strip 302 u under the hit: jump into the spring (hit on tick 18, momentum.y -575), release, double jump on input 19 (tick 20, Velocity.y 745): the dot hovers at y 222.7-237.8 until the second hit on tick 26 (momentum.y -1054.9), then falls 32.1 and 32.7 u a tick through the strip (in it on ticks 36 and 37 only) into the finish box on tick 40. The same inputs without the double jump (one hit) cross the strip at 25.3-26.9 u a tick and die on tick 34. Sideways: the injected spring-double-hit-side lab map (offline): walk under a spring pointing right with a wall in front of it and jump; hits on ticks 27 and 35 (momentum.x 4800, then 8781.3), over the wall on tick 38, over a 4200-wide spike strip and into the finish box on tick 83. Jumping from further back enters the trigger higher: one hit, death in the strip on tick 78.

name: Spring dash stack
description: A straight-down dash through a second down spring stacks both springs' momentum. The dash moves momentum into preDashMomentum and zeroes it (1643-1644), so nothing decays for its ticks; the spring hit mid-dash calls endDash first (hitSpring 2436-2439), which gives back 95% of preDashMomentum.y when its sign matches the dash's (2035-2037), then adds the spring's momentum and sets Velocity.y (2474-2477). After the Course 5 ceiling spring (-575) the second hit leaves momentum.y -1109 and Velocity.y -270; a plain fall through the same spring gets -1013.4, 3 ticks later. A down or flat dash that ends in the air hits the dash-end brake instead: endDash sets Velocity.y to 10 whenever it is under 10 (2024-2027). Works for sideways and upward springs too (endDash gives back the momentum along the dash's sign): a flat spring dash between two sideways springs gives momentum.x 9255, and an up-right dash between two up springs gives momentum.y 1803.8. The main demo is the downward case; the spring-dash-stack-side and spring-dash-stack-up labs are the others. The second spring must end the dash before the first spring's movementLock runs out: its cancelSpringCutscene Invoke still fires mid-dash and sets cutsceneMode none, and after that endDash gives nothing back (see spring-dash).
note: Demonstrated on the injected spring-dash-stack lab map (WJ_DS_BS_ZIP_OM, offline): jump into spring-clip's ceiling spring (tick 18), dash straight down on input 19 (33.4 u a tick on ticks 20-26) into a second down spring under the ledge: the hit on tick 27 (momentum.y -1109.0, Velocity.y -270), then 34.1 and 34.7 u a tick through a 32-tall spike strip (in it on ticks 39 and 40 only) into the finish box on tick 42. Ghosts: the dash aimed down-right misses the second spring and ends on tick 31 with Velocity.y +10 and momentum.y -522.1 (the dash-end brake), crossing the strip at 25.3-27.0 u a tick and dying on tick 53; no dash falls through the second spring (tick 30, momentum.y -1013.4) and finishes on tick 46. Sideways: spring-dash-stack-side lab (offline): the hit on tick 17, a spring dash (springDash 1, lockX 1) from tick 19 level at y 49.2, the second spring on tick 26 (momentum.x 9255), over a spike strip to the finish on tick 69; no dash: over the second spring and into the strip. Upward: spring-dash-stack-up lab: the hit on tick 17 (momentum.y 925), dash up-right on input 18, the second spring on tick 24 (momentum.y 1803.8), peak y 2277, finish on tick 68; no dash: peak y 1511.5.

name: Landing jump keeps downward momentum
description: OnCollisionStay2D zeroes Velocity.y and momentum.y on a (0, 1) floor contact but returns first while recentlyJumped is on (2518-2526), and a ground jump turns recentlyJumped on for 0.03 s (1685-1687). A jump buffered for the landing tick (pressed up to 6 ticks before) leaves on the tick the ground rays land the dot, so that tick's floor contact keeps momentum.y: landing with a down spring's momentum (-366 left of the Course 5 ceiling spring's -575 after 20 ticks) the jump leaves at 805 against it and the momentum carries into the next drop. A jump one tick later finds momentum.y zeroed. Not the same as landing-tick-jump, which is about ground friction on momentum.x.
note: Demonstrated on the injected landing-jump-momentum-carry lab map (NONE, offline): the hit on spring-clip's ceiling spring (tick 18), a fall onto a ledge 200 u below the start with jump pressed on input 32 (5 ticks early) and released on 33: the landing tick 38 jumps with Velocity.y 805 and momentum.y -365.7 kept (peak y -102.4), then stick right and down off the ledge's edge: below y -600 on tick 77 and in the finish box (under y -1000) on tick 90. Jumping one tick late (input 38, momentum zeroed on the landing tick, a full jump, peak -36.1) is 8 ticks behind at y -600 (tick 85) and finishes on tick 100; landing and walking off the edge is below -600 on tick 80 and finishes on tick 95.

name: Jump-through buy
description: A jump carrying the stick's sideways momentum whose arc passes two adjacent shop boxes buys both on the way (each box's buy trigger only needs the player inside it; the 0.2 s buy cooldown is per box), instead of walking into one and then the other. From a box spot it is a short hop along the box row; from a quick restart's landing, the gate or the finish it is the arc that ends the walk in.
note: Measured by fulltas-buytable on FalseEnding-Any% (390.38 base, 2026-09-29): jump-through was the fastest way found for 52 of 339 Course 2 entries and 70 of 275 Course 3 entries. From the buyreward2 spot, buyclone2 then buyclonemult2 in one jump took 30 ticks against 44 chaining the two single walks (23 + 21); from buyclonemult2, buyglobalreward2 then buyds 32 against 47; from buyclonemult3, buyclonemult3 then buyfast3 25 against 68. Seeds: jumps held 6 or 14 ticks with the stick full sideways after run-ups of 0-24 ticks, both directions (FullTasBuyTable.cs PassSeeds). The buy planner (tools/plan-buytable.py) emits such a pair as one buy:a+b goal.

name: Dash-through buy
description: A dash along a row of shop boxes buys every box its pass touches (each box's buy trigger only needs the player inside it; the 0.2 s buy cooldown is per box), instead of walking into one box and then the next.
note: Measured by fulltas-buytable on FalseEnding-Any% (390.38 base, 2026-09-29), Course 3 (reward:bonus3 .. buy:buystatue, caps wjds): of 207 ordered pairs measured with both, the dash pass was faster than the best walk or jump-through for 55. From the buyclonemult3 spot, buyreward3 then buystatue took 56 ticks less by dash; from Course 3's restart landing, buyglobalreward3 then buyclone3 39 less. Seeds: a run-up of 0-24 ticks then a dash along the row with the stick held, both directions (FullTasBuyTable.cs PassSeeds).

name: Record-break payout
description: A course finish that beats the course's best time (courseScript.stopTracking: currentPathTime < bestPathTime) replaces the clone path (clonesScript.updateClonePath), which destroys every clone still on the old path (DestroyClone), and each one pays its full reward on the spot: the course reward × (2 × bigness + 1) × the clone mult (0.1 + 0.2 per global cloneMult + 0.1 per local), comp boost included, plus its red or green power. On the current game build (25630570, 2026-09-30) the on-screen pool runs full: a clone spawns into every free slot each rendered frame, so min(cloneCount, its lifetime in frames) are in flight, and a course with 52 clones pays about 52 clone payouts at the finish on top of the finish's own reward. The pool then refills at one clone a frame, so the new path pays the full ratio of the two best times (Course 2 2.20 -> 1.90 s: +15.7 % income). Nothing is lost: each of those clones would have paid at the end of its path within one best time anyway, so the break only moves that cash earlier, by up to one best time. A record can be broken only by a strictly faster finish, so a run can save one: finish an earlier lap 1 physics tick (0.02 s) slow, and when a big upgrade is a few clone payouts short, run the full-speed lap to break the record and buy it right away. Back to back (a ladder of known laps from the quick restart, slowest first), each break catches the refilled pool just after it paid: about cloneCount x (1 - restart overhead / new best time) payouts, about 38 for Course 2's 52 clones at 1.9 s.
note: Only clones on the path pay. A course's clones stay where they were, hidden, while it is off screen, and a course that has paid off screen with clones loses Start's 10000 s on its spawn timer: after a break it refills over about one best time, and a break pays about half its clones. The scuff costs the tick it gave up, plus a path 0.02 s longer (clone income down 0.02 / bestPathTime) until the break. A prestige that resets clone time (courseScript.onPrestige, bestPathTime 1E+11) makes the next finish a record anyway. On the pre-2026-09-30 build a clone spawned every bestPathTime / cloneCount rounded up to whole frames and the pool ran short (Course 2's 52 at 2.20 s: 50 in flight), so a faster path paid less (+9.9 % for 2.20 -> 1.90 s). The ladder is a planning model, pending measurement; the model: docs/fulltas.md "Clones and buy-max (build 25630570)". The offline engine models the break (Economy.CourseFinished; its spawns are the old build's until the port lands), and fulltas --auto's goals part plays it (payout breaks, enginesim/Cli/FullTasAutoPayout.cs, docs/fulltas.md "Auto"): the laps that set or tie the best time a tick slower, and a later lap breaking it, the record lap played again when that lap is slower.

name: Wall coyote restart
description: Full-TAS use of checkpoint-midair-walljump: a quick restart (Movement.respawn) zeroes Velocity and momentum and puts the dot on the ground, but leaves wallCoyoteFrames and wallJumpsLeft alone, and the ground branch never counts wallCoyoteFrames down. So a wall cling just before the restart, or any cling followed only by ground ticks, starts the next lap with a stored wall jump: the lap's first ground jump, then a jump press on the 2nd-6th tick after it (wallCoyoteFrames still above 0) is a wall jump off no wall, Velocity (460 away from the way the dot faces, 730 up) with the 7-tick lock, or the superbounce's boost within 5 ticks of a dash. The ground jump always comes first (jumpBuffer && onGround is checked before the wall branch, and the restart sets onGround), so the trick is an extra jump in the lap's first ticks, never a replacement for the lap's first jump. It needs the unlock (buywj), a wall reachable just before the restart, and its ticks paid before it: enginesim's --parts wallreset grafts it around a run's quick restarts.
note: Measured offline (2026-09-30). Lab (checkpoint-midair-walljump.graft.demo.json, the default demo's inputs with a graft spec): cling at input 24 (wallCoyoteFrames 7), quick restart on input 25 (count 7 and wallJumpsLeft 4 kept, OnWall off, onGround on, the count holds on the ground), ground jump on 28 (Velocity.y 805, it comes first), the count then reads 6, 5, 4, 3, 2; the jump pressed on 34 (count 1 at the check) is a wall jump off no wall, Velocity (-460, 730); on 36 it doesn't fire. On FalseEnding-Any% (360.17 s, fulltas --wallreset-study): 157 quick restarts, 107 after buy:buywj (the unlock), nearly all in mid-air right after a buy; 7 already carry a count (Course 3's buyreward3 row, a cling at 9200,7084 before goals 179, 220, 223 and 244, then the restarts 7 ticks later with 1-2 left); none of the 157 has a stick hold toward a wall on its last 1-10 ticks that leaves a count (0 of 3,140), so a run gets the count only by another way into the box. Grafted by fulltas --auto --parts wallreset (enginesim/Cli/FullTasAutoWallReset.cs, docs/fulltas.md "Parts"): the spec'd windows sit at TouchedWall and LeftWall (the stick into the wall 3 ticks, the restart, 0-3 idle ticks, the ground jump held 1-4, the wall jump, then the run's stick). The loop's gain from it is not measured yet.
